ANSWER: The guard lives in two files:

**`pkg/okf/provenance.go` — `ensureNoForgedHumanVerification` (line 26)**
This is the enforcement function. It receives the `actor` string (the identity performing the save). If the actor is **not** a human identity (`IsHumanIdentity(actor)` returns false — which is the case for agents like the MCP server), it loads the verifications already recorded on disk and then walks every `Verified` entry on the concept being saved. If any entry has a human `By` field that was **not already on disk** (i.e. it is newly added), it returns an error:
```
actor %q cannot add human verification %q
```
This prevents a non-human actor from injecting a new human-authored verification entry.

**`pkg/okf/mutate.go` — `saveConceptLocked` (line 476)**
This is the save path that calls the guard. At line 494, before writing anything to disk, it calls:
```go
if err := ensureNoForgedHumanVerification(fullPath, c, actor, opts.IsNew); err != nil {
    return err
}
```
If the actor comes in blank (e.g. the MCP server passes no actor), it defaults to `"agent/okf-tool"` (line 492), which `IsHumanIdentity` will not recognise as human, so the guard is active for all agent-originated saves.

The public entry point `SaveConcept` (line 459) delegates to `saveConceptLocked`, so any caller — including the MCP server — goes through this check.

CONFIDENCE: high
